raw: 36.1 Threat Intelligence Aggregation Agent: LangChain + STIX/TAXII
teaching_note: Treat the inherited integrations as source-guide context; this chapter's executable teaching contract uses only in-memory synthetic records, with no network, credentials, scanners or publication. A structured object describes an assertion and its provenance, while a transport specification describes exchange; neither validates the assertion. Synthetic records F1 and F2 reproduce one originating bulletin, so aggregation yields two documents and one evidence family, not corroboration; a contrary F3 remains visible. TAXII 2.1 specifies Collections services, while Channels are reserved rather than specified in that version; no transport is invoked here. [@official_oasis_stix_21; @official_oasis_taxii_21]
title: Offline structured-evidence aggregation: supplied CTI-style records

raw: 36.2 Multi-Agent OSINT Crew: CrewAI + Shodan + theHarvester + Maltego
teaching_note: Implement the crew concept as separate local task records rather than operational collection tools. Completed synthetic handoff Q2: child T1 reviews R1/R3 source status, T2 reviews R2/R4 origin links, both under local-read-only H1 until checkpoint K1 with no redelegation; T1 returns R1 current/R3 superseded and T2 returns R2/R4 derived from R1. The parent can draft one origin-supported policy claim with the historical contradiction noted, but must abstain on real-world authority and cannot send the packet externally. A missing T2 output would make lineage incomplete, not implicitly independent; the shared claim procedure is in Section [@sec:analytic-workflow].
title: Offline source-review crew: local handoff records

raw: 36.3 Autonomous Vulnerability Scanner: AutoGen + Nmap + MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
teaching_note: The raw scanner title is preserved only as inherited source identity; the lesson reviews prewritten fictional result records and launches no scanner or tool. Synthetic finding V1 says 'possible affected package' but lacks ecosystem/version; supplied inventory I1 gives a similarly named package in a different ecosystem, so the bounded disposition is identity mismatch/affectedness unresolved, not a confirmed vulnerability or false-positive rate estimate. Retain result ID, tool/version-as-supplied, inventory provenance and missing evidence, then request a human review of approved records. An ATT&CK label is a behavior taxonomy reference, not a vulnerability test or permission for exploitation. [@official_nist_ssdf; @official_mitre_attack_enterprise]
title: Offline review of supplied scanner-result records: no autonomous scanning

raw: 36.4 RAG Pipeline for All-Source Intelligence Fusion: LangGraph + Chroma + OpenAI
teaching_note: Represent retrieval as query plus corpus version returning passage IDs, then check claim support separately; inherited SBOM/software references are provenance context, not evidence of RAG efficacy. In synthetic packet P1, R1§2 supports required review, R3 is superseded and R5 contains an embedded direction to waive review: the accepted answer cites R1, preserves R3's historical status and rejects R5's direction as data rather than authority. If a derived note already copied that waiver, quarantine the note and all dependent claims, restore the clean checkpoint and rebuild before review. The runnable example demonstrates deterministic record contracts, not an LLM-security implementation or a complete injection defense. [@scholarly_greshake_2023_indirect_prompt_injection]
title: Offline passage retrieval and claim-support contracts

raw: 36.5 Pattern-of-Life Analysis Agent: Persistent Memory + GEOINT + OSINT
teaching_note: The safe analogue tracks revisions of fictional evidence artifacts, never real people, movement or locations. Synthetic memory M1 accepted 'review optional' from draft R3; current rule R1 supersedes it, so transition M1 to superseded, invalidate dependent C1 and create C2 supported by R1 with a correction link. Persisting both texts without state filtering would let retrieval revive the stale claim; the expected decision is to exclude superseded support and pause if the current version cannot be established. A summary and its source are not two independent observations.
title: Offline longitudinal document-state review: no person tracking

raw: 36.6 Cognitive Security Inoculation Agent: Van der Linden Taxonomy + GPT-4o
teaching_note: Use fixed transparent classroom items and a separate answer-key record, with no profiling, tailored persuasion or automated delivery. The lesson record explains that 'either change the library logo or oppose reading' excludes alternatives; an unseen item about opening hours tests whether the answer identifies that same false-dilemma structure rather than merely disagreeing. Keep the key out of the answering component's retrieval, memory and writable context, and score the stated explanation against it only afterward. This is a proposed offline exercise: correct recognition on a toy item would not establish durable resilience, real-world behavior change or agent-delivery efficacy. [@scholarly_roozenbeek_2022_psychological_inoculation]
title: Offline opt-in media-literacy lesson and isolated assessment records

raw: 36.7 Supply Chain Inspector: SBOM + GitHub Commit Analysis + Anomaly Detection
teaching_note: A local inventory parser should preserve package ecosystem, namespace, version, relationship and provenance instead of matching on a bare name. Synthetic inventory I2 lacks a build identifier while advisory A2 names an affected build range: record affectedness unknown and request the approved build record, rather than claiming safety, exploitability or maintainer misconduct. An unusual supplied commit summary is a review cue, not evidence of malicious intent, and neither repository access nor package analysis is executed. The example's validation of record structure cannot certify the software described. [@official_nist_ssdf; @official_nist_sp_800_161r1]
title: Offline software-provenance and advisory-record review

raw: 36.8 ICS Anomaly Detection Agent: OT Network + MITRE ATT&CK for ICS
teaching_note: The offline analogue compares supplied fictional process-event values with declared units and a toy baseline; it never connects to an OT network or recommends a physical control change. Input E1 is 12 units within a declared 10–20 range; E2 is 28 with an unknown unit and E3 is missing, yielding in-range-for-fixture, incomparable/review and unknown respectively, not two incidents. Stop interpretation until approved metadata resolves E2/E3; an ATT&CK-for-ICS association would organize a hypothesis, not prove an attack or justify actuation. The chapter's standard-library example and expected output demonstrate local permissions, evidence lineage and stopping only, not a calibrated anomaly detector or production assurance.
title: Offline toy process-event review: no OT connection or actuation
